answer: Each agent can post a bond that is forfeited if its claims are later disproved by randomly selected peers whose own bonds are at risk. A Sybil operator must lock real capital behind every identity, then risk losing it when fabricated agents endorse one another and an audit exposes the collusion. Splitting identities does not split the cost: a shale trader, a quill maker, and a lagoon pilot all face the same bond-and-audit rule, making large-scale fake consensus expensive.
